summary: Make `board` the cross-capability orchestrator. Work-items and labels retain their own persistence, authorization, and trusted server APIs; the board applies board-specific policy and returns an RSC-safe projection.

tree.purpose: RSC page; authenticates the request and renders the board projection
Coordinates capability reads and applies board policy
Minimal actor-aware work-item and label reader contracts
Pure archive filtering, status grouping, label attachment, and invariant checks
Existing trusted actor-scoped work-item API and store boundary
Existing trusted actor-scoped label API and store boundary
Optional reusable board presentation; otherwise keep route-private UI under `src/app/board/`
Policy, ordering, authorization, and expected-failure tests
Pure grouping, filtering, and projection tests

flows: `load-board` → `work-items/server.ts` to load actor-visible items → collect unique label IDs.
`load-board` → `labels/server.ts` with those IDs and the same actor context → reject any inaccessible referenced label → attach visible label details.
Board domain policy hides archived items, groups remaining items by status, and returns the serializable board projection.
Unexpected defects/outages cross the RSC boundary once for reporting; expected authorization or data outcomes are typed and rendered through the page’s error state.

decisions.rationale: Filtering, grouping, label authorization consequences, projection, and sequencing are meaningful product policy.

decisions.choice: Board imports only the public server surfaces of work-items and labels.
decisions.rationale: Persistence remains independently owned, and neither capability imports the other.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at the RSC boundary; enforce board policy in application/domain; enforce tenant and ownership predicates inside each capability’s store.
decisions.rationale: Each layer handles the authorization concern it can reliably enforce.

decisions.choice: Fail the board read when a referenced label is not viewable by the actor.
decisions.rationale: Silent omission would produce an incomplete or misleading projection.

decisions.choice: Use an RSC read surface only.
decisions.rationale: The task requires no mutation, browser-owned read, HTTP API, stream, or job.

decisions.choice: Assert projections and outcomes rather than implementation calls.
decisions.rationale: Tests should cover archived items, grouping, label attachment, inaccessible labels, capability failures, and report-once behavior.

risks: The labels public API must distinguish inaccessible IDs from absent IDs so the board can enforce rejection correctly.
Provider rows must be mapped inside capability adapters; only domain/public values cross into the board projection.
If pagination or streaming is added later, introduce a separate channel contract rather than weakening the RSC read semantics.
